en: The Discourse on the Ten Branches Spoken by the Buddha to the Householder of Aṭṭhakanāgara, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, a number of senior bhikṣus were staying at Pāṭaliputra.

Not long after the Blessed One had entered parinirvāṇa at the Kukkutārāma monastery, many wealthy householders from Daśagrāmaka in Aṣṭakulaka went to Pāṭaliputra to engage in trade. Thereupon, the householders from Daśagrāmaka in Aṣṭakulaka purchased all the goods with their money and wealth; having purchased them all, they were exceedingly joyful, and having gained great profit, they felt extreme delight and immense gladness of heart.
Having departed from the city of Pāṭaliputra and arrived at the Kukkuṭārāma, he approached the elder bhikṣus, prostrated at their feet, and sat down to one side.

The householder Daśamaṇika of Aṣṭagrāmaka also sat down to one side. Then the elder bhikṣus taught the Dharma to him, exhorting him, encouraging him, instructing him, and guiding him; through manifold skillful means they taught the Dharma, exhorting him up to the point of complete guidance. Having brought him to a state of joy, they remained silent.

Then, having heard the Dharma taught by those venerable bhikṣus and being encouraged toward the ultimate joy, the ten householders from the branch city and the people of Aṭṭhakanāgara addressed those venerable bhikṣus, saying:
“Venerable sirs!...”
"Where is the Venerable Ānanda staying now?
I wish to see him.
"O householder! [he replied.]
"That venerable Ānanda is at the Monkey’s Pond in Vaiśālī; those who wish to see him should go there.

Thereupon, the lay follower Daśamaṇava of Aṣṭagrāma rose from his seat, prostrated at the feet of the senior bhikṣus, circumambulated them, and departing from the seniors, returned to where the venerable Ānanda was.
Having arrived, he prostrated at the feet of the Venerable Ānanda and sat down to one side.
Once the householder Daśoṭṭhaka of Aṭṭhakanāgara was seated to one side, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying: "Ānanda!..."
"I wish to ask something; please grant me leave to ask.
"Ask, householder!"
Having heard this, he understood it:
"Venerable Ānanda!

Does that Blessed One—who possesses wisdom and vision, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha—teach with his own eye the foremost truth a single Dharma, wherein a noble disciple abides, such that there is the liberation of the mind through the exhaustion of taints in this very life?"
"Householder! That Blessed One is wise and possessed of vision;

he is the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. With his own eye, he perceives the ultimate truth and teaches a single Dharma in which the noble disciple abides, wherein there remains a further state for the exhaustion of the outflows and the liberation of the mind."
"Venerable Ānanda, how is it that the Tathāgata, the Arhat,

the Perfectly Enlightened One, having seen the ultimate truth with his own eyes, taught a single Dharma in which noble disciples abide, and through which there is the remainderless exhaustion of taints and liberation of mind?"

"O householder! It is possible that a noble disciple, having heard [the teaching], attains liberation from sensual desire and dwells in the attainment of the four dhyānas; that he, relying on the practice of contemplating the characteristics of phenomena as they enter the Dharma, dwells in that practice of contemplating the characteristics of phenomena as they enter the Dharma;
and that while dwelling therein, he may attain the destruction of the outflows (āsrava-kṣaya), whereas he does not attain the destruction of the outflows by not dwelling therein."

Delighting in the Dharma himself, loving the Dharma himself, practicing the Dharma himself, and revering the Dharma himself, he attains joy; with the five lower fetters exhausted, he attains rebirth by transformation, attains parinirvāṇa there as a non-returner (anāgāmin), and does not return to this world.
"In this way, householder, that Blessed One—

possessing wisdom and vision, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha— perceiving with his own eyes the ultimate truth, teaches a single Dharma in which noble disciples abide, wherein there remains a further state for the exhaustion of taints and the liberation of the mind."

Furthermore, householder! When a noble disciple has heard [the teaching], he dwells having attained meditative absorption (samāpatti), with a mind imbued with loving-kindness (maitrī) pervading one direction; likewise the second, third, and fourth directions, above, below, and all around—everywhere. With a mind imbued with loving-kindness, free from enmity, free from duality, free from ill will, vast, exalted, immeasurable, and thoroughly developed, he dwells having attained meditative absorption pervading all directions. Likewise, with a mind imbued with compassion (karuṇā), sympathetic joy (muditā), and equanimity (upekṣā), he dwells having attained meditative absorption pervading all directions. For one who dwells thus, relying on the practice of the contemplation of the characteristics of phenomena as they enter [the mind], it is possible that, by dwelling therein, he may attain the destruction of the outflows (āsravakṣaya).

Not abiding in that place, one attains the exhaustion of outflows; if, through the joy of the Dharma and the love of the Dharma, one practices reverence for the Dharma and attains the Dharma of rapture, then with the five lower fetters exhausted, one attains birth by transformation and attains parinirvāṇa in that very place as a non-returner (anāgāmin), no longer returning to this world.
This is it, householder!

That Blessed One is wise and possessed of vision; he is the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. He perceives the ultimate truth with his own eyes and proclaims the supreme Dharma—the dwelling place of noble disciples wherein, in this very life, there is the remainderless exhaustion of the outflows and liberation of the mind.
Furthermore, householder! Regarding what a noble disciple has heard:

having transcended all perceptions of form, he dwells in the meditative attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. By relying on the practice of contemplating the characteristics of phenomena within the entry into those states, he proceeds until the exhaustion of the outflows and the liberation of the mind.
Thereupon, the householder Daśaśaila of Aṣṭāpada addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
"How extraordinary, Venerable Ānanda! How marvelous!"
We asked the Venerable Ānanda about one gate of the deathless, yet he has explained twelve gates of the deathless for us.
It is truly much,
Venerable Ānanda!
Regarding these twelve gates of ambrosia, one should, by means of each respective gate of ambrosia, conduct oneself with peace and security.
It is just so, Venerable Ānanda!

Not far from the city and village there is a multi-storied pavilion; by the side of this multi-storied pavilion there are twelve doors. There may be someone who enters it for some minor purpose, or someone who gives rise to thoughts that are meaningless, unbeneficial, insecure, and unhappy, or there may be someone who sets fire to the multi-storied pavilion. This, Venerable Ānanda!
That person, through these twelve gates, exits at ease according to their own will.
How truly marvelous this is,
Venerable Ānanda!
We asked the Venerable Ānanda about one gate to the Deathless, yet he has explained twelve gates to the Deathless for us.
O Venerable Ānanda!
This is truly much; regarding these twelve gates to the Deathless, one should emerge from each through its respective gate to the Deathless.
"Venerable Ānanda!
Do those brahmins give gifts to their teachers while being possessed of evil qualities?"
"How much more so now that we are before the Great Teacher—should we not provide him with material offerings?
Thereupon, the ten householders of Aṭṭhakanāgara prepared pure and exquisite food and drink that very night.
That night, having prepared pure and exquisite food and drink, he arranged seats at the appropriate time.
Having arranged the seats, he invited the community of bhikṣus from the Kukkuṭārāma and the community of bhikṣus from Vaiśālī, and they all assembled together.
Once the community of bhikṣus at Kukkuṭārāma and the community of bhikṣus at Vaiśālī had all assembled, he personally served them with pure and exquisite food and drink with his own hands.

Having personally served him pure and exquisite food with his own hands, and knowing that he had finished eating, he collected the bowls and utensils, provided water for washing, and purchased a house with five hundred kinds of goods to offer as a private residence to the Venerable Ānanda.
That venerable Ānanda bestowed it upon the Saṃgha of the four quarters.
Thus spoke the venerable Ānanda.
Having heard what the venerable Ānanda had said, the lay follower Daśamaṇavaka of Aṭṭhakanāgara rejoiced and was glad.
The Sūtra on the Householder Daśaśākha of Aṣṭāpada Spoken by the Buddha.
